message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta’s local council (or the relevant municipal office). Here’s how you can do it:

1. **Locate the correct department**  
   • In many cities, noise complaints are handled by the Code Enforcement Office, the Police Department’s Traffic Division, or a dedicated Noise Control Unit.  
   • For Atlanta, you’ll usually start with the City’s Code Enforcement Office or the Atlanta Police Department’s Traffic Division.

2. **Gather details**  
   • Date and time of the disturbance.  
   • Exact location (address or intersection).  
   • Description of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs).  
   • Any evidence you have (photos, videos, audio recordings).

3. **File the complaint**  
   • **Online:** Many municipalities offer an online portal or web form for noise complaints. Search “City of Atlanta noise complaint” on the official city website.  
   • **Phone:** Call the city’s non-emergency line or the specific department’s hotline.  
   • **In person:** Visit the city hall or the Code Enforcement Office during business hours.  

4. **Follow up**  
   • After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy for future correspondence.  
   • If you don’t hear back within a reasonable timeframe, follow up using the reference number.

5. **Know the regulations**  
   • Most cities have ordinances specifying quiet hours (often 10 p.m.–7 a.m.) and acceptable decibel limits. Familiarizing yourself with those can strengthen your case when you file.

If you’re unsure which department handles noise complaints in your specific neighborhood, you can also ask at the local community center or check the city’s official website for a “Contact Us” page that lists departments and phone numbers.
